guarantees.claim: cipher_op is combinational and resolves to CIPH_INV only for (AES_ECB,AES_DEC) and (AES_CBC,AES_DEC); for all other mode/op combinations it is CIPH_FWD.

formal.consequent: cipher_op == ((aes_mode_q == AES_ECB && aes_op_q == AES_DEC) || (aes_mode_q == AES_CBC && aes_op_q == AES_DEC)) ? CIPH_INV : CIPH_FWD

formal_sketch.consequent: cipher_op == ((aes_mode_q == AES_ECB && aes_op_q == AES_DEC) || (aes_mode_q == AES_CBC && aes_op_q == AES_DEC)) ? CIPH_INV : CIPH_FWD

guarantees.claim: cipher_op_buf is logically equivalent to cipher_op (via prim_buf and type cast), guaranteeing no value change through the buffering

assumptions.claim: ctr_incr and iv_q must satisfy the protocol and timing requirements of the aes_ctr sub-module (not enforced here)
assumptions.risk: violation may cause incorrect counter increment, leading to wrong keystream and security compromise

formal_sketch.consequent: ctr_incr and iv_q must satisfy the protocol and timing requirements of the aes_ctr sub-module (not enforced here)

uncertain_points.claim: If aes_mode_q or aes_op_q hold values outside the listed enumerations, cipher_op silently defaults to CIPH_FWD without error indication.
uncertain_points.cond: when mode/op is not among supported enums
uncertain_points.risk: could allow unintended forward operations, potentially corrupting data or leaking plaintext

formal.antecedent: !(aes_mode_q inside {AES_ECB, AES_CBC, AES_CFB, AES_OFB, AES_CTR}) || !(aes_op_q inside {AES_ENC, AES_DEC})

formal_sketch.antecedent: !(aes_mode_q inside {AES_ECB, AES_CBC, AES_CFB, AES_OFB, AES_CTR}) || !(aes_op_q inside {AES_ENC, AES_DEC})

uncertain_points.claim: ctr_alert is wired directly to the output without local latching or qualification; proper handling depends entirely on external logic.
uncertain_points.risk: security alert may be missed or delayed, allowing continued operation under fault

formal_sketch.consequent: ctr_alert is wired directly to the output without local latching or qualification; proper handling depends entirely on external logic

security_implications: The chunk sets cipher operation direction via cipher_op, defaulting to CIPH_FWD for unknown modes, which could silently allow incorrect operations and compromise confidentiality/integrity. The direct output of ctr_alert from the AES-CTR counter without internal handling poses a risk of unhandled security alerts, potentially allowing unsafe operation during faults.
